claim_1.claim: Hemagglutination Inhibition analysis of plasma from 212 TIV-vaccinated subjects across the 2007–2011 seasons showed that day 28 antibody responses decreased significantly with increasing age, while no significant differences were detected by gender, diabetic status, or race.

sources.quote: We evaluated the plasma antibody responses of all vaccinated individuals via hemagglutination-inhibition (HAI) antibody titer assays.

In the 2010 and 2011 seasons, in which elderly subjects were included, antibody responses showed a significant decrease with age ( Figures 1B , 1C , and S1C ), consistent with previous studies ( Seidman et al., 2012 ).
There was no significant difference in antibody response based on gender ( Figure S1D ), diabetic status ( Figure S1E ), or race (data not shown).
A total of 212 subjects were vaccinated with TIV during the 2007–2011 influenza seasons.

comparison.finding: day 28 antibody responses decreased significantly with increasing age

claim_2.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from TIV vaccinees across multiple seasons showed that interferon and dendritic-cell blood transcriptional modules at days 1 and 3 after primary vaccination (day 1 and day 3) and ASC/cell-cycle modules at day 7 after primary vaccination (day 7) were positively associated with day 28 HAI responses, whereas T-cell modules at days 1 and 3 after primary vaccination (day 1 and day 3) were negatively associated.

sources.quote: BTMs related to the induction of interferons as well as the activation of dendritic cells ( Figures 2A and 2B ) were enriched on days 1 and 3 after TIV vaccination, whereas modules related to T cells at these time points were negatively associated with the antibody response.
On day 7, there was a robust enrichment of ASC and cell cycle-related modules, consistent with our original study ( Nakaya et al., 2011 ).
Blood samples were collected at baseline and on days 3, 7, 28, and 180 days after vaccination.

Total RNA from PBMCs (~1.5 × 10 6 cells) was purified using Trizol (Invitrogen, Life Technologies Corporation) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Samples were checked for purity and hybridized on Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays (Affymetrix).

comparison.finding: Interferon and dendritic-cell blood transcriptional modules at days 1 and 3 after primary vaccination were positively associated with day 28 HAI responses, whereas T-cell modules at days 1 and 3 were negatively associated.

claim_3.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from young and elderly TIV vaccinees showed that module-level signatures at day 3 and day 7 after primary vaccination (day 3 and day 7) predicted day 28 HAI high versus low responders with 79.0%–80.2% accuracy in young test sets and 64.7%–72.3% accuracy in elderly test sets, with frequently selected modules involving innate immune responses, leukocyte differentiation, antigen presentation, B cell/immunoglobulin production, and cell cycle pathways.

sources.quote: With this approach, we identified BTMs that predicted HAI responses in both the young and elderly groups with accuracies ranging between 79.0% and 80.2% and between 64.7% and 72.3%, respectively, using both day 3 and day 7 signatures ( Figure 2C ).

Examination of the modules most frequently selected by the algorithm in the 100 randomized trials revealed pathways related to innate immune cell responses as well as leukocyte differentiation and antigen presentation on day 3 and B cell/immunoglobulin production and cell cycle pathways on day 7 ( Table S3 ).
Blood samples were collected at baseline and on days 3, 7, 28, and 180 days after vaccination.

comparison.finding: At day 3, module-level signatures predicted day 28 HAI high versus low responders with higher accuracy in young test sets (79.0%–80.2%) than in elderly test sets (64.7%–72.3%); frequently selected modules involved innate immune responses, leukocyte differentiation, and antigen presentation.

At day 7, module-level signatures predicted day 28 HAI high versus low responders with higher accuracy in young test sets (79.0%–80.2%) than in elderly test sets (64.7%–72.3%); frequently selected modules involved B cell/immunoglobulin production and cell cycle pathways.

claim_4.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of baseline PBMCs from combined influenza vaccine studies showed that pre-vaccination B-cell- and T-cell-related modules were positively correlated with stronger day 28 HAI responses, whereas monocyte-related modules were negatively correlated; the negatively associated monocyte modules included TLR4, TLR8, NOD2, ASGR2, IFN-γR, IL-13R, TIMP2, LYN, and SYK.

sources.quote: This approach revealed several B-cell- and T-cell-related modules whose expression pre-vaccination was positively correlated with an increased antibody response to vaccination in all studies ( Figure 3A ).
In contrast, modules related to monocytes were negatively correlated with antibody responses ( Figures 3B – 3G ).

Interestingly, contained within the monocyte-related modules were genes such as TLR4 , TLR8 , NOD2 , and ASGR2 , which encode proteins involved in innate sensing, and genes encoding IFN-γR, IL-13R, TIMP2, LYN, SYK, and other molecules involved in inflammation.

Total RNA from PBMCs (~1.5 × 10 6 cells) was purified using Trizol (Invitrogen, Life Technologies Corporation) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Samples were checked for purity and hybridized on Human U133 Plus 2.0 Arrays (Affymetrix).

claim_5.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from the 2010 and 2011 cohorts showed that increasing age was associated with higher NK-cell-related module expression at day 3 and day 7 after primary vaccination (day 3 and day 7) and higher monocyte-module expression at day 7 after primary vaccination (day 7), whereas many B-cell modules decreased with age at both timepoints.

sources.quote: Natural killer (NK) cell-related modules showed increased expression with age on both day 3 and day 7 after vaccination, and several monocyte modules showed increased expression with age on day 7.
In contrast, many B cell modules showed decreased expression in older subjects on both day 3 and day 7.
Blood samples were collected at baseline and on days 3, 7, 28, and 180 days after vaccination.

comparison.finding: increasing age was associated with higher NK-cell-related module expression and lower B-cell module expression at day 3
increasing age was associated with higher NK-cell-related module expression, higher monocyte-module expression, and lower B-cell module expression at day 7

claim_6.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that elderly subjects had higher total NK-cell proportions than young subjects at baseline and throughout days 0–14 after primary vaccination (day 0–14), with vaccination increasing NK-cell percentages in the elderly but reducing them in the young at day 1 after primary vaccination (day 1).

sources.quote: Our analysis showed that proportions of total NK cells in elderly subjects were higher than those of young subjects at baseline as well as at all the time points studied (days 0–14).

Of note, vaccination induced an increase in the percentage of NK cells in the elderly subjects; in contrast, in the young there was a reduction in the percentage of NK cells on day 1 after vaccination ( Figure 5A ).
In order to distinguish between these two possibilities, we performed FACS analysis on PBMCs in a subset of subjects from the 2010 cohort.
2–3 × 10 6 PBMCs were thawed and stained with live/dead marker (Alexa Fluor 430, Life Technologies) to exclude dead cells.

comparison.finding: elderly subjects had higher total NK-cell proportions than young subjects at baseline
elderly subjects had higher total NK-cell proportions than young subjects at day 1 after primary vaccination
elderly subjects had higher total NK-cell proportions than young subjects at day 14 after primary vaccination
vaccination increased NK-cell percentages in the elderly at day 1 versus baseline
vaccination reduced NK-cell percentages in the young at day 1 versus baseline

claim_7.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that elderly subjects had a higher frequency of CD56dim CD16++ NK cells and a lower frequency of CD56++ NK cells at baseline than young subjects; after primary vaccination (day 0), CD56dim CD16++ cells increased significantly in the elderly at day 1 (day 1), while CD56++ cells increased in the young at day 7 (day 7).

sources.quote: We observed a higher frequency of CD56 dim CD16 ++ cells coincident with a lower frequency of CD56 ++ cells in the elderly at baseline, consistent with previous studies ( Figure 5C ; Solana et al., 2014 ).

The distribution of these subpopulations was relatively stable during the response, with CD56 dim CD16 ++ cells showing a small but significant increase in the elderly on day 1 after vaccination and CD56 ++ cells increasing in the young on day 7.
Blood NK cells were defined within the live singlets gate CD3 − CD4 − CD19 − CD14 − cells as the CD56 ++ NK, CD56 ++ CD16 + NK, and CD56 dim CD16 ++ NK.

comparison.finding: at baseline, elderly subjects had a higher frequency of CD56dim CD16++ NK cells and a lower frequency of CD56++ NK cells than young subjects
in elderly subjects, CD56dim CD16++ NK cells increased significantly at day 1 vs baseline after primary vaccination
in young subjects, CD56++ NK cells increased at day 7 vs baseline after primary vaccination

claim_8.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that CD69 activation of all three NK-cell subsets increased after primary vaccination (day 0) in elderly subjects and peaked at day 3 (day 3), whereas young subjects showed lower activation limited to the CD56dim CD16++ subset at day 1 (day 1).

sources.quote: Elderly subjects showed increasing activation after vaccination in all three subsets, with highest expression on day 3.
In contrast, the young exhibited activation of the CD56 dim CD16 ++ subset as measured by CD69 expression only on day 1 and at a lower level than in the elderly.
Blood NK cells were defined within the live singlets gate CD3 − CD4 − CD19 − CD14 − cells as the CD56 ++ NK, CD56 ++ CD16 + NK, and CD56 dim CD16 ++ NK.

comparison.finding: In elderly subjects, CD69 activation increased after primary vaccination across all three NK-cell subsets and peaked at day 3.
Young subjects showed lower CD69 activation than elderly subjects, and this activation was limited to the CD56dim CD16++ NK-cell subset at day 1.

claim_9.claim: microRNA profiling assay analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees measuring 672 human miRNAs at days 1, 3, and 7 after primary vaccination (day 1, day 3, and day 7) showed distinct age-related responses, with predominantly upregulated differentially expressed miRNAs in elderly subjects, especially at days 1 and 7 (day 1 and day 7), versus predominantly downregulated miRNAs in young subjects.

sources.quote: To assess whether or not miRNAs contribute to the differences in response we saw between young and elderly vaccinees, we measured the miRNA expression profiles of 672 human miRNAs on days 1, 3, and 7 after vaccination from a subset of subjects in the 2010 cohort ( Figure 7A ).

We saw a significant difference in the miRNA profiles between these two groups. Whereas a majority of the differentially expressed miRNA in the elderly were upregulated after vaccination, particularly on days 1 and 7, the young exhibited predominantly downregulation of miRNA.
For a subset of the 2010 season cohort, fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) measurements as well as miRNA profiling were also performed ( Figure 1A ).

comparison.finding: At day 1, elderly subjects showed predominantly upregulated differentially expressed miRNAs, whereas young subjects showed predominantly downregulated miRNAs.

At day 3, miRNA profiles differed significantly between young and elderly vaccinees, with elderly showing predominantly upregulated differentially expressed miRNAs and young showing predominantly downregulated miRNAs.
At day 7, elderly subjects showed predominantly upregulated differentially expressed miRNAs, whereas young subjects showed predominantly downregulated miRNAs.

claim_10.claim: microRNA profiling assay analysis of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that miRNAs correlated with day 28 HAI responses differed by age group, with elderly subjects having a larger number of miRNAs negatively correlated with antibody response than young subjects.

sources.quote: We also identified miRNA whose expression correlated with the day 28 antibody response ( Figure 7B ).
We again saw differences between the young and elderly subjects, with the elderly having a larger number of miRNA negatively correlating with the antibody response when compared with the young.

comparison.finding: miRNAs correlated with day 28 HAI antibody responses differed by age group, with elderly subjects having a larger number of miRNAs negatively correlated with antibody response than young subjects

claim_11.claim: microRNA profiling assay integrated with transcription profiling by array of PBMCs from a subset of 2010 TIV vaccinees showed that day 1 after primary vaccination (day 1) miRNA-BTM correlations implicated regulation of the antiviral interferon module M75, with miR-424 predicted to target OAS3 and CXCL10.

sources.quote: We then performed correlation analysis between all miRNA-BTM pairs, revealing groups of modules that appear to be regulated together by several miRNA ( Figure 7D ) on day 1 after vaccination.

Of particular interest was the regulation of module M75-antiviral interferon signature ( Figure 7E ) on day 1 after vaccination, because the interferon pathway plays a key role during the innate immune response.

This miRNA-mRNA network suggests potential novel regulators of the interferon response after vaccination, such as miR-424. This miRNA was predicted to target OAS3, a 2′–5′-oligoadenylate synthase involved in viral RNA degradation ( Samuel, 2001 ), as well as CXCL10, an important chemokine induced by IFN-γ that serves as a chemoattractant for lymphocytes ( Dufour et al., 2002 ).

groups.assay_method: microRNA profiling assay integrated with transcription profiling by array
